title: Contract Pricing Agreement Escalation Conditions for Contract Item Prices
content:
# Escalation of contract item prices — Contract Pricing Agreement

**E1. Price lock.** No contract item is escalated with an effective date earlier than the tier's price lock, in calendar months, after the agreement effective date. Add the months to the agreement effective date by calendar month; when the target month has no such day the boundary is the last day of that month, and an escalation effective on the boundary date is allowed. The agreement effective date is the one on the agreement record.

**E2. Notice.** An escalated price takes effect no earlier than the tier's escalation notice period, in calendar days, after the escalation notice date. Count notice days starting the day after the escalation notice date; a price effective on the last notice day is allowed. The notice date is the one recorded on that item's price line.

**E3. Amount of an escalation — no longer in force (superseded by the current basis).** Retired: "An escalation raises a contract unit price by the percentage increase in Corbett's supplier cost for that item since the item's previous price line, capped at the tier's annual escalation cap percent of the prior contract unit price, and each item is escalated at most once in any 12 months; a supplier cost decrease never lowers a fixed contract price."

**E4. Cost-plus tier.** On the Cost-Plus tier there is no fixed price to escalate: a supplier cost increase changes the cost-plus price the tier's supplier cost change notice period, in calendar days, after its notice date, and a supplier cost decrease changes it from the next ship date.

**E5. Tiers with no contract items.** A tier with no contract items has nothing to escalate; its prices follow Corbett list price changes from the list effective date.

| Boundary (hypothetical figures) | Allowed |
|---|---|
| Lock of 6 months, agreement effective 31 August: escalation effective 28 February in a year whose February has 28 days (the last day of that month, which has no 31st) | Yes, on the boundary date |
| Same lock: escalation effective 27 February | No, earlier than the boundary |
| Notice of 30 days: price effective on day 30 counted from the day after the notice date | Yes, the last notice day |
| Same notice: price effective on day 29 | No |

superseded_clauses: An escalation raises a contract unit price by the percentage increase in Corbett's supplier cost for that item since the item's previous price line, capped at annual_escalation_cap_pct percent of the prior contract unit price, and each item is escalated at most once in any 12 months; a supplier cost decrease never lowers a fixed contract price.
